sources.citation: Lovestrand, Joseph. 2026. Directional extensions in Chadic languages. Berlin: Language Science Press.
sources.note: Appendix on East Chadic B1: 'The description of Zerenkel (zire1244) is a work in progress, but the relevant data is not available at the moment.' Thanks Sakine Ramat (for Migaama). No Zerenkel phonology.

sources.citation: SIL International. Resources for language zrn (Zerenkel) — sil.org/resources/search/language/zrn, Internet Archive copy 2015-09-17.
sources.note: Bibliographic listing only: 15 items = Johnson 2005 survey (2 records) + 13 Zerenkel primers, readers, calendars and arithmetic booklets (FAPLG/SIL, 2007-2011, all 'Not Online'). No phonology or grammar listed; Ramat's works are not in the SIL public catalogue. No post-2015 Internet Archive copy exists; live sil.org is an automated-access block-walled by automated download.

sources.citation: Lovestrand, Joseph. 2013. East Chadic B: classification and description progress report. Journal of West African Languages 40(1): 105-130.
sources.note: pp. 113-114: Zerenkel listed under 'unpublished preliminary analyses' (Ramat 2007, 2011, SIL N'Djamena manuscripts); the appendix wordlist gives Zerenkel forms from Johnson 2005 (e.g. kume 'animal', gapi 'horn', kuɾuki 'ten') with no tone or stress marks, whereas neighbouring Kajakse/Birgit forms do carry tone and stress marks. Nothing on Zerenkel prosody.

sources.citation: Lovestrand, Joseph. 2012. Classification and description of the Chadic languages of the Guéra (East Chadic B). SIL Electronic Working Papers 2012-004. Dallas: SIL International. 59 pp.
sources.note: Comparative segmental survey; no prosody/tone/stress section for any language. On Zerenkel: p. 13 'A fourth language, Zerenkel, has been analyzed by a member of the Fédération des Associations pour la Promotion des Langues du Guéra (FAPLG) in cooperation with SIL (Ramat 2007, 2011)'; p. 24 prenasalized plosives (only Guéra language with them); p. 27 complex onset [bla] 'vomiting' (Ramat 2007); p. 48 consonant and vowel charts 'Source: Ramat 2007, 2011' (i/ii e/ee a/aa o/oo u/uu). Nothing on Zerenkel stress or tone. Bibliography: Ramat, Sakine. 2007. Notes d'essai de description de la langue z…

sources.citation: Johnson, Eric. 2005. Étude sociolinguistique de la langue Zirenkel du Tchad. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2005-023. Dallas: SIL International. 30 pp.
sources.note: Sociolinguistic survey (Nov 2000). Sec. 4 'La langue zirenkel' (p. 7) opens: 'Puisqu'aucune recherche linguistique n'a été entreprise sur la langue zirenkel'; gives only lexicostatistics (71% with Mubi, 34-36% with Dangaléat dialects) and says there are no dialects. Annexe B (pp. 14-20) is a 227-item wordlist in segmental IPA (SILDoulosIPA93 font) with no stress marks and no tone marks on the Zirenkel column (page 15 image checked). Nothing on stress, accent, tone or prosody.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page zire1244 (Zirenkel); Wikipedia en 'Zirenkel language' and fr 'Zirenkel'; Wikidata Q3441365
sources.note: Glottolog lists only the two Ramat items as descriptive references plus Johnson 2005 for endangerment. Wikipedia stubs cite Ethnologue and Johnson 2005 only; no phonology, tone or stress information anywhere.

sources.citation: Ramat, Sakine (data) in Chan, Eugene S. L. (comp.). 2014. Zerenkel. Numeral Systems of the World's Languages. Leipzig: Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology,https://lingweb.eva.mpg.de/channumerals/Zerenkel.htm(data dated 10 October 2014).

sources.note: No statement about tone anywhere on the page. The Zerenkel numerals supplied by Sakine Ramat (10 Oct 2014) are transcribed with acute and grave diacritics on many but not all forms (pínné 1, siirí 2, sùbbà 3, páɗɗá 4, bíƴƴá 5, bèèsiri 7, paarpaɗì 8, paarpinò 9, kúrúkí 10, rakí in 11; but istala 6 and the second members of compounds - suba, paɗa, siri, paarpaɗi, wer - are unmarked), i.e. the describer writes Zerenkel with tone-type accents, consistent with a pitch contrast of at least two heights, but the marking is partial and the page gives no analysis, inventory or statement; evidence of to…

sources.note: The only book-length description (Glottolog listed by Glottolog as a grammar sketch); a 191-page description-to-orthography study almost certainly has a phonology chapter that settles whether Zerenkel is tonal and whether stress is mentioned. Hammarström's Glottolog record names a PDF, so a copy exists; ask Harald Hammarström, Joseph Lovestrand (who calls it a work in progress) or SIL Chad / University of Buea.
